stemBlocks.value: $18 000 is invested at 5% per annum compound interest, compounded annually for 3 years. a. Calculate the amount at the end of 3 years.  b. Calculate the compound interest earned.
Think first: Find the amount first; the interest is whatever the amount exceeds the original investment by.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p017-q07 from workbook page 17.

solutionSteps.instruction: Turn the rate into a multiplier.
Subtract the principal to get the interest.

strategyBlocks.value: Multiply $18 000 by 1.05 three times, then subtract the principal from the result.

whyThisWorks.value: Each year's balance is 105% of the year before, so three years multiply the principal by 1.05 three times over. Compound interest is never a single percentage of the principal; it is the amount at the end minus the amount at the start, because later years earn partly on earlier interest. Simple interest here would give only $2 700, and the $137.25 difference is interest on interest.
